emergency.notes: Tourist Police: 196. Jordan Civil Defence: 199. Emergency response in Amman is reliable. In rural areas and Wadi Rum desert, response times can be long.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise increased caution in Jordan due to terrorism and armed conflict near its borders. Jordan is generally more stable than its neighbors but the volatile regional environment poses risk. Avoid areas near the Syrian and Iraqi borders.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Most visits to Jordan are trouble-free. Be aware of the volatile regional situation. Petrol bombs and protests occur occasionally. Take care near Syrian and Iraqi borders.

healthcare.costForTourists: Healthcare in Jordan is good quality and affordable by Western standards. Clinic visit $30-70. Emergency room $100-400. Private hospital stay $200-600/night. Jordan is actually a medical tourism destination for the region.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies (saydaliat) are widely available. Many medications available OTC. English widely spoken at pharmacies.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Private hospitals in Amman are of good quality. Jordan University Hospital is the main teaching hospital. Specialty Hospital caters to international patients. English is widely spoken in the medical sector.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance with medical coverage recommended. Jordan has good medical infrastructure. Medical evacuation coverage recommended for adventure activities (Wadi Rum, Dead Sea).

controlledSubstances.note: Carry original prescription with doctor's letter. Jordan customs can be strict. Declare at customs. Max 30-day supply.
Require original prescription. Keep in original packaging.
Cannabis is illegal in Jordan. Penalties are severe.

medications.generalAdvice: Jordan has relatively strict customs procedures for medications. Always carry medications in original packaging with a doctor's letter and copies of prescriptions. Declare all medications at customs.

scams.name: Petra guide overcharging
scams.description: Unofficial guides at Petra offer 'better than official' tours at lower prices. They often don't show you the major sites and demand more money mid-tour.
scams.avoidance: Use only licensed guides from the Petra official visitor center. Book in advance through reputable tour operators.

scams.name: Carriage and donkey ride overcharging
scams.description: Horse and carriage operators, and donkey ride guides inside Petra, charge tourists inflated prices and may not disclose the fare until the ride is complete.
scams.avoidance: Negotiate and confirm the exact price in Jordanian Dinar before accepting any ride. Prices should be posted at official stands.

scams.name: Dead Sea resort overcharging
scams.description: Beach resorts at the Dead Sea have inconsistent pricing for day visitors, with some adding charges for towels, showers, and access that were not disclosed upfront.
scams.avoidance: Ask for a full breakdown of all charges before entering. Many resorts have standardized day-pass prices — confirm this covers all facilities.

connectivity.simOptions: SIM cards from Zain, Orange Jordan, or Umniah at the airport and phone stores. Tourist SIM ~JD 10-20 ($14-28) for 5-15GB. eSIM via Airalo.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi in hotels, cafes, and restaurants in Amman. Limited in Petra and Wadi Rum. Most heritage sites have patchy connectivity.
connectivity.bestOption: Zain Jordan SIM for best coverage including desert and rural areas.

cultural.tipping: Expected in restaurants (10%), hotels (JD 1-2/day for housekeeping), taxis (round up), and for guides (JD 5-10 per day). Jordan has a tipping culture influenced by tourism.
cultural.dressCode: Modest dress expected outside tourist areas and hotels. Women should cover shoulders and knees in cities, mosques, and conservative areas. Men should avoid shorts in traditional neighborhoods. Swimwear only at hotel pools and beaches.
cultural.greetings: Men shake hands with men. Women may extend a hand to men but this is not universal — follow the lead of the Jordanian. 'Marhaba' (hello) and 'As-salamu alaykum' (peace be upon you) are warmly received.
taboos: Entering mosques without permission or inappropriate dress
Photography of military installations, government buildings, or uniformed personnel
Public criticism of the King or Royal Family
Drinking alcohol in public outside licensed establishments
Eating or drinking in public during Ramadan daytime
cultural.haggling: Expected at souks and with unofficial vendors. Not practiced in supermarkets or official stores. Start at 50-60% of asking price.

safety.lgbtSafety: Homosexuality is technically legal (decriminalized in 1951) but same-sex relationships are not recognized and LGBTQ+ individuals face significant social discrimination. Exercise extreme discretion.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Moderate. Jordan is safer for women than many regional neighbors. Harassment does occur, particularly in rural areas. Modest dress reduces but does not eliminate attention. Group or guided travel recommended for women in conservative areas.
safety.notes: Jordan is one of the most stable and tourist-friendly countries in the Middle East. The main security concerns are regional spillover from neighboring conflicts and occasional protests. Tourist areas (Petra, Wadi Rum, Dead Sea, Aqaba) are generally well-managed and safe.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: visa on arrival or e-visa (JD 40, included in Jordan Pass). UK, EU, Australia: visa on arrival. Jordan Pass includes entry to 40+ sites including Petra.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: March-May and September-November for comfortable temperatures. Avoid June-August (extreme heat 40°C+). Wadi Rum is spectacular at dawn and dusk year-round.

hospitals.name: Jordan University Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main teaching hospital affiliated with the University of Jordan.

hospitals.name: Specialty Hospital
hospitals.notes: Private hospital catering to international patients. Full English-speaking staff.

immediate: Never attempt to cross flooded wadis (dry riverbeds that flood rapidly) — flash floods are extremely dangerous
Move to high ground immediately if you hear rushing water or see rapidly rising water
Do not enter flooded areas even in 4WD vehicles — water depth is deceptive
If camping in a wadi, move to high ground immediately at the first sign of rain, even distant rain
Do not park in or near wadis during rainy season
after: Wait for the Jordan Meteorological Department all-clear before crossing any wadi
Check road conditions with authorities before traveling
Avoid Petra's Siq (narrow canyon) during or after heavy rain — flash floods are a documented danger

immediate: Stay hydrated — drink at least 3 liters of water per day
Avoid outdoor activities between 11am and 4pm in summer
Seek shade and air conditioning during the hottest hours
Recognize heat stroke symptoms: hot dry skin, confusion, lack of sweating — call ambulance immediately
after: Monitor weather forecasts from Jordan Meteorological Department
Check on vulnerable travelers in your group
